Below is a complete empirical research plan tailored to your data, timing, and institutional setting.

## 1. Identification Strategy

I will use a two-tier empirical strategy:

A. Variety-level difference-in-differences with event-study (Sun-Abraham) to estimate the causal effects of (i) U.S. statutory import tariffs on import variety outcomes (HS10-by-origin-by-month) and (ii) foreign retaliatory tariffs on U.S. export variety outcomes (HS10-by-destination-by-month). This design exploits sharp, discrete, and staggered policy changes at fine product–country–time cells, using untreated varieties of the same product-month and other products within the same origin/destination-month as controls, while absorbing rich high-dimensional shocks.

B. Shift-share (Bartik-style) panel DID for sectoral and county outcomes to quantify distributional and general-equilibrium-relevant effects. Exposures are constructed from predetermined 2016 input-output/exports and mapped to sectors (NAICS-4) and counties via pre-tariff employment shares. This leverages cross-sectional heterogeneity in ex-ante exposure to a common national tariff shock over time.

Why this works:
- The policy is plausibly exogenous at the level of individual variety-months, arrives in sharp waves, and is discriminatory across origins/destinations—creating powerful within-product cross-origin variation ideal for DID/event studies with rich fixed effects.
- For distributional/welfare incidence, the relevant margin is how sectors and places differ in pre-existing connections to tariffed inputs and retaliated export markets. A shift-share panel DID with sector/county and month fixed effects appropriately summarizes this heterogeneity.

## 2. Treatment and Control

A. Import-side analyses (U.S. statutory tariffs)
- Unit of observation: HS10 product p imported from origin o in month t.
- Treatment variable: Statutory ad valorem tariff rate τ_pot in percent (or indicator 1[τ_pot>0]) applied to imports from origin o in product p and month t.
- Treatment timing: First month the new statutory tariff becomes effective for (p,o). Multiple waves: 2018-02 (solar/washers), 2018-03 (steel/aluminum), 2018-07/08/09/… (China lists). We code start dates per product-origin-month.
- Control group: Untreated origins for the same product-month (i.e., other o′ shipping product p in month t that did not face the tariff), plus untreated products for the same origin-month (o-by-t). Identification leverages within-product-month and within-origin-month contrasts.

B. Export-side analyses (retaliatory tariffs on U.S. exports)
- Unit of observation: HS10 product p exported to destination d in month t.
- Treatment variable: Retaliatory ad valorem tariff rate ρ_pdt in percent (or indicator) applied by destination d on imports from the U.S. of product p in month t.
- Treatment timing: First effective month from the foreign measures (China, Canada, Mexico, EU, Russia, Turkey; 2018 waves by list).
- Control group: Untreated destinations for the same product-month (other d′), plus untreated products for the same destination-month.

C. Sector/county exposure (distribution and welfare)
- Sector exposure to import tariffs (inputs): For sector s, Exposure_input_st = Σ_p w^IO_sp × τ_pt, where w^IO_sp is the 2016 cost share of HS product p in sector s’s intermediate input bundle (from BEA IO tables), aggregated to HS–NAICS via concordances.
- Sector exposure to retaliation (exports): Exposure_export_st = Σ_{p,d} w^{X}_{spd,2016} × ρ_pdt where w^{X}_{spd,2016} is sector s’s 2016 export share in p-to-d.
- County exposure: Map sector exposures to county c using 2016 employment shares: Exposure_input_ct = Σ_s emp_share_cs,2016 × Exposure_input_st; Exposure_export_ct analogously. Optionally separate protection (import-side) vs retaliation (export-side).
- Outcomes: Sectoral IP, PPI/MPI/XPI, and county wages/employment/income.

No RDD is proposed (no natural running variable/cutoff suitable for a local design), and no IV is strictly necessary for the micro DiD; we rely on rich FE and pre-trend diagnostics. If desired, an IV extension could use list-based inclusion as instrument for tariff incidence in robustness.

## 3. Key Identifying Assumptions

A. Variety-level DID/event study
- Parallel trends within product-month across treated vs untreated origins (imports) and within product-month across treated vs untreated destinations (exports), absent the tariffs.
  Plausibility: Tariffs were sharply imposed and discriminatory, and including product×month FE absorbs common demand/supply shocks at the product level; origin×month (or destination×month) FE absorb origin/destination-wide shocks. Remaining differential pre-trends at the origin within product can be probed with dynamic leads and origin-product-specific trends.
- No substantial anticipatory behavior beyond modeled leads.
  Plausibility: There was some advance signaling; event windows with leads and possibly excluding the month immediately pre-implementation address inventory pull-forward.
- SUTVA/local interference: Effects on untreated origins for the same product reflect substitution. Our estimand is the effect on the treated pair; substitution does not bias the treatment-on-the-treated but complicates general equilibrium aggregation. For welfare, we incorporate substitution via IO/shift-share and reallocation checks.

B. Shift-share sector/county DID
- Exogeneity of shocks interacted with predetermined weights: Conditional on sector/county and time FE, differences in 2016 input/export structure are orthogonal to time-varying shocks driving outcomes.
  Plausibility: Weights are pre-period; policy design targeted product lists largely for policy/political goals, not to contemporaneous sectoral performance conditional on FE. We will implement many-ingredient exposure with AKM-style inference and leave-one-out weights to reinforce credibility.
- Limited re-optimization of weights in the short run: Short-run is appropriate (2017–2019) given limited capacity to rewire supply chains immediately.

## 4. Threats to Identification and Mitigation

1) Endogenous targeting and differential pre-trends within product-origin/destination
- Mitigation: Dynamic event-study with pre-treatment leads and origin-product (or product-destination) linear trends; placebo tests using pre-2018 pseudo-treatment dates; saturation with product×month and origin×month FE; sample restriction to balanced traders (positive flows pre-period) to avoid entry-driven biases.

2) Anticipation/stockpiling and measurement error in unit values
- Mitigation: Include event-time leads to estimate anticipatory spikes; robustness excluding k∈{-2,-1,0} months around implementation; winsorize/truncate extreme unit values; weight by baseline values/quantities; use duties collected to construct tariff-inclusive/exclusive prices; complement with sectoral PPIs/MPI/XPI.

3) Concurrent policy and macro shocks (steel quotas, sanctions, exchange rates)
- Mitigation: Origin×month FE absorb exchange rate and macro shocks; product×month FE absorb commodity/demand shocks; control for product-specific global prices (if available); robustness excluding metals/energy subsets most affected by quotas; destination×month FE in export regressions.

For the shift-share:
- Correlated exposure due to large shocks (e.g., China lists) creating weak effective number of shocks
  Mitigation: AKM/jackknife standard errors; aggregate shocks by list×rate cells and cluster; randomization inference by permuting list assignment over products within HS sections.

## 5. R Code Outline

Note: This is an executable outline assuming plausible file names and variable names. You may need to adapt concordances and variable names.

```r
# Packages
library(data.table)
library(fixest)       # feols, sunab, fepois
library(lubridate)
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)

# 1) Load data
imports <- fread("imports_variety_month.csv")   # columns: hs10, origin, month, customs_value, quantity, duties_collected
exports <- fread("exports_variety_month.csv")   # columns: hs10, dest, month, customs_value, quantity, duties_collected
tariff_us <- fread("us_tariffs_hs10_origin_month.csv")  # hs10, origin, month, stat_tariff # in percent
tariff_ret <- fread("retaliation_tariffs_hs6_dest_month.csv") # hs6, dest, month, ret_tariff
hs10_to_hs6 <- fread("hs10_to_hs6.csv") # hs10, hs6
prod_map <- fread("hs_to_naics4.csv")   # hs10, naics4
io <- fread("io_2016_hs_naics_costshares.csv") # naics4, hs10, io_share
exports_2016 <- fread("exports_2016_hs10_dest_naics.csv") # naics4, hs10, dest, export_share_2016
sector <- fread("sector_month.csv")     # naics4, month, ip, ppi, mpi, xpi
county_emp <- fread("county_sector_emp_2016.csv") # fips, naics4, emp_share_2016
county_out <- fread("county_month.csv") # fips, month, wages, employment, income
votes <- fread("county_votes_2016.csv") # fips, trump_share_2016

# Parse dates
for(dt in list(imports, exports, tariff_us, tariff_ret, sector, county_out)) {
  dt[, month := ym(month)]
}

# 2) Merge tariffs into variety panels
# Imports: merge statutory tariff at hs10-origin-month
imp <- merge(imports, tariff_us, by = c("hs10","origin","month"), all.x = TRUE)
imp[is.na(stat_tariff), stat_tariff := 0]

# Compute unit values; careful with zeros
imp <- imp[quantity > 0 & customs_value > 0]
imp[, uv := customs_value / quantity]
imp[, ln_qty := log(quantity)]
imp[, ln_uv := log(uv)]
imp[, ln_val := log(customs_value)]

# Treatment timing/event time per hs10-origin
imp[, treat_start := month[which.max(stat_tariff > 0)], by = .(hs10, origin)]
imp[, ever_treated := as.integer(any(stat_tariff > 0)), by = .(hs10, origin)]
imp[, rel_time := as.integer(interval(treat_start, month) / months(1))]
# Cap event time for Sun-Abraham
imp[, rel_time_c := pmin(pmax(rel_time, -6L), 12L)]

# Exports: merge retaliation tariffs at hs6-dest-month via hs10->hs6
exp <- merge(exports, hs10_to_hs6, by = "hs10", all.x = TRUE)
exp <- merge(exp, tariff_ret, by = c("hs6","dest","month"), all.x = TRUE)
exp[is.na(ret_tariff), ret_tariff := 0]

exp <- exp[quantity > 0 & customs_value > 0]
exp[, uv := customs_value / quantity]
exp[, ln_qty := log(quantity)]
exp[, ln_uv := log(uv)]
exp[, ln_val := log(customs_value)]

exp[, treat_start := month[which.max(ret_tariff > 0)], by = .(hs10, dest)]
exp[, ever_treated := as.integer(any(ret_tariff > 0)), by = .(hs10, dest)]
exp[, rel_time := as.integer(interval(treat_start, month) / months(1))]
exp[, rel_time_c := pmin(pmax(rel_time, -6L), 12L)]

# 3) Main variety-level regressions

# Imports: event study of ln_qty on treatment using Sun-Abraham (sunab)
# FE: product x month, origin x month, and product x origin (the last is implicit in sunab cohort FE)
# Use feols with sunab(ever_treated, rel_time_c)
est_imp_qty <- feols(ln_qty ~ sunab(ever_treated, rel_time_c),
                     data = imp,
                     fixef = ~ hs10^month + origin^month + hs10^origin,
                     cluster = ~ hs10^origin + month)
summary(est_imp_qty)
iplot(est_imp_qty, ref.line = 0)

# Imports: pass-through to unit values
est_imp_uv <- feols(ln_uv ~ sunab(ever_treated, rel_time_c),
                    data = imp,
                    fixef = ~ hs10^month + origin^month + hs10^origin,
                    cluster = ~ hs10^origin + month)
summary(est_imp_uv)
iplot(est_imp_uv, ref.line = 0)

# Alternative intensity spec: continuous tariff rate
est_imp_qty_tau <- feols(ln_qty ~ stat_tariff,
                         data = imp,
                         fixef = ~ hs10^month + origin^month + hs10^origin,
                         cluster = ~ hs10^origin + month)
summary(est_imp_qty_tau)

# Exports: event study of retaliation on export ln_qty and ln_uv
est_exp_qty <- feols(ln_qty ~ sunab(ever_treated, rel_time_c),
                     data = exp,
                     fixef = ~ hs10^month + dest^month + hs10^dest,
                     cluster = ~ hs10^dest + month)
summary(est_exp_qty)
iplot(est_exp_qty, ref.line = 0)

est_exp_uv <- feols(ln_uv ~ sunab(ever_treated, rel_time_c),
                    data = exp,
                    fixef = ~ hs10^month + dest^month + hs10^dest,
                    cluster = ~ hs10^dest + month)
summary(est_exp_uv)

# Robustness: PPML on quantities/values to handle zeros and heteroskedasticity
imp_ppml <- fepois(quantity ~ stat_tariff | hs10^month + origin^month + hs10^origin, data = imp)
summary(imp_ppml)

# 4) Construct sector and county exposures

# Sector input exposure: join io shares to tariffs at hs10-month; aggregate
imp_tariff_hs10m <- unique(imp[, .(hs10, month, stat_tariff)])
io_exp <- merge(io, imp_tariff_hs10m, by = "hs10", allow.cartesian = TRUE)
io_exp[, input_exposure := io_share * stat_tariff]
sector_input_exp <- io_exp[, .(Exposure_input = sum(input_exposure, na.rm=TRUE)), by = .(naics4, month)]

# Sector export exposure: join 2016 export shares to ret tariffs
ret_tariff_hs10dm <- unique(merge(hs10_to_hs6, tariff_ret, by = "hs6")[, .(hs10, dest, month, ret_tariff)])
x_exp <- merge(exports_2016, ret_tariff_hs10dm, by = c("naics4","hs10","dest"), allow.cartesian = TRUE)
x_exp[, export_exposure := export_share_2016 * ret_tariff]
sector_export_exp <- x_exp[, .(Exposure_export = sum(export_exposure, na.rm=TRUE)), by = .(naics4, month)]

# Combine exposures and merge with sector outcomes
sector_exp <- merge(sector_input_exp, sector_export_exp, by = c("naics4","month"), all = TRUE)
sector_exp[is.na(Exposure_input), Exposure_input := 0]
sector_exp[is.na(Exposure_export), Exposure_export := 0]
sector_panel <- merge(sector, sector_exp, by = c("naics4","month"), all.x = TRUE)
sector_panel[is.na(Exposure_input), Exposure_input := 0]
sector_panel[is.na(Exposure_export), Exposure_export := 0]

# Sector-level DID: outcome on exposures with sector and month FE
est_sec_ip <- feols(ip ~ Exposure_input + Exposure_export | naics4 + month, data = sector_panel, cluster = ~ naics4)
summary(est_sec_ip)

# County exposures
sec_exp_for_county <- sector_exp
county_exp <- merge(county_emp, sec_exp_for_county, by = "naics4", allow.cartesian = TRUE)
county_exp[, Exposure_input_c := emp_share_2016 * Exposure_input]
county_exp[, Exposure_export_c := emp_share_2016 * Exposure_export]
county_month_exp <- county_exp[, .(Exposure_input = sum(Exposure_input_c, na.rm=TRUE),
                                   Exposure_export = sum(Exposure_export_c, na.rm=TRUE)), by = .(fips, month)]

county_panel <- merge(county_out, county_month_exp, by = c("fips","month"), all.x = TRUE)
county_panel[is.na(Exposure_input), Exposure_input := 0]
county_panel[is.na(Exposure_export), Exposure_export := 0]

# County outcomes on exposures
est_cnty_inc <- feols(income ~ Exposure_input + Exposure_export | fips + month, data = county_panel, cluster = ~ fips)
summary(est_cnty_inc)

# 5) Political economy: association between county exposure and 2016 vote
cnty_pol <- county_month_exp[month == ym("2019-04")]
cnty_pol <- merge(cnty_pol, votes, by = "fips")
pol_reg <- feols(Exposure_input + Exposure_export ~ trump_share_2016 + log(population_2016) | state, data = cnty_pol, cluster = ~ state)
summary(pol_reg)

# 6) Robustness checks

# (a) Pre-trend test: average of leads in event study should be ~0
etable(est_imp_qty, keep = "sunab::lead", dict = c("sunab(ever_treated, rel_time_c)::" = "k="))

# (b) Exclude months [-1,0,+1] around treatment to mitigate stockpiling
imp_noring <- imp[!(rel_time %in% c(-1,0,1))]
est_imp_qty_noring <- feols(ln_qty ~ sunab(ever_treated, rel_time_c) | hs10^month + origin^month + hs10^origin,
                            data = imp_noring, cluster = ~ hs10^origin + month)
summary(est_imp_qty_noring)

# (c) Add origin-product-specific linear trends
imp[, tindex := as.integer(month - min(month)), by = .(hs10, origin)]
est_imp_qty_trend <- feols(ln_qty ~ sunab(ever_treated, rel_time_c) + i(tindex, df=1) | hs10^month + origin^month + hs10^origin,
                           data = imp, cluster = ~ hs10^origin + month)
summary(est_imp_qty_trend)
```

Notes:
- fixest’s sunab handles heterogeneous timing properly.
- FE notation hs10^month is an interaction fixed effect (two-way saturated).
- Consider weighting micro regressions by pre-period variety import value to stabilize influence.

## 6. Expected Results

- Imports:
  - Quantities: Negative response for treated origin-product pairs; back-of-envelope elasticities suggest a 25 pp tariff reduces own-origin import quantities by roughly 30–50% in the short run for differentiated goods; less for highly inelastic inputs. Expect substitution toward untariffed origins within the same HS10.
  - Prices (unit values): Positive pass-through to landed import prices, but incomplete for pre-tariff (exporter) prices; near-complete for tariff-inclusive purchaser prices. Expect pre-tariff import unit values to rise by 10–20% for a 25% tariff (some absorption by foreign exporters).
- Exports under retaliation:
  - Quantities: Declines, especially in agriculture; a 25 pp retaliatory tariff could reduce U.S. export quantities by 20–40% in targeted HS lines in the short run.
  - Prices received by U.S. exporters likely decline modestly (negative pass-through), especially in commodities.
- Sectoral/county outcomes:
  - Sectors intensive in tariffed imported inputs: higher input costs, softer IP; some protected sectors (steel/aluminum) may show IP/price increases.
  - Counties specialized in export-targeted sectors (farm-heavy) see weaker income/employment; input-tariff-exposed manufacturing counties face cost pressure.
- Aggregate real income: Net negative in the short run after accounting for higher import costs and retaliatory losses, partially offset by tariff revenue; likely modest but nontrivial negative share of GDP in this horizon.
- Political patterns: Retaliation targeted toward politically salient U.S. constituencies (agriculture-heavy, higher Trump vote share); U.S. protection may correlate with swing-state or politically connected sectors.

## 7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID/event study)

- C1: Credible parallel trends supported by rich FE and pre-trend tests — 1
- C2: No major anticipatory behavior unmodeled (we include leads/exclusions) — 0.5
- C3: No confounding concurrent shocks within product×month and origin/dest×month (absorbed by FE) — 1
- C4: Accurate treatment timing and measurement (statutory schedules, official retaliation lists) — 1
- C5: Appropriate inference and robustness (clustering, PPML, trends, robustness windows) — 1

Total: 4.5/5

This plan yields causal estimates of short-run trade-flow and price effects and maps them to sectoral and geographic distribution, while transparently assessing political correlates of protection and retaliation.
